Title: Age-Associated Proteomic Signatures and Potential Clinically Actionable Targets of Colorectal Cancer
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Paired Colorectal Cancer (CRC) tumor tissues and adjacent non-cancerous tissues
Tissue: Colorectal tumor and adjacent normal tissue
Disease Subtype: Age-stratified CRC: young <41 years (n=22); middle-aged 41–60 years (n=12); old >60 years (n=16)
Experimental Design: Paired tumor (T) versus matched adjacent normal tissue (N); 50 patients; 12 TMT10-plex batches containing 6–10 biological samples per batch; technical duplicate analysis of eight pairs (P009–P012 and P028–P031); age-group comparison
Short Description: TMT 10-plex quantitative proteomic profiling of 50 paired CRC tumor/adjacent tissues to identify age-associated proteomic signatures
Normalization Strategy: Within-batch total intensity normalization; T/N ratio calculation (adjusted protein intensities)
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C). Variable: Oxidation (M); Acetylation (Protein N-term)
Main_Finding: Age-associated enhancement of MYC, E2F and G2M-checkpoint protein signatures was observed in colorectal tumors, with substantially greater tumor-versus-adjacent-normal proteomic differences in older patients; NHP2 was identified as an age-associated prognostic and potentially actionable protein target.
Data_Caveats: Adjacent normal tissues were obtained from the same CRC patients rather than from separate healthy donors; GYQ013 and GYQ032 occur in primary batch sheets but are absent from the final clinical annotation, with the reason for exclusion Not specified; no bridge/reference channel or additional cross-batch normalization was reported
Quantification_Format: Linear normalized protein intensities; paired T/N ratios calculated downstream

Title: Proteotranscriptomics of ocular adnexal B-cell lymphoma reveals an oncogenic role of alternative splicing and identifies a diagnostic marker
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Frozen human orbital/ocular adnexal tissue specimens from 39 patients with ocular adnexal B-cell lymphoma: 27 EMZL/MALT lymphoma, 8 DLBCL, 2 MCL and 2 CLL/SLL; 15 inflammatory non-cancer controls: 9 idiopathic orbital inflammation and 6 reactive lymphoid hyperplasia specimens; and 11 normal orbital tissue controls
Disease Subtype: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue, EMZL/MALT lymphoma (n=27); diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, DLBCL (n=8: 7 non-GCB and 1 GCB); mantle cell lymphoma, MCL (n=2); chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma, CLL/SLL (n=2)
Experimental Design: Observational case–control proteotranscriptomic study. The original cohort comprised 71 patients/specimens: 40 OABL, 12 IOI, 6 RLH and 13 normal orbital tissues. Six specimens were excluded from proteomics because of plasma-protein contamination. The final proteomic cohort contained 65 individual samples: 39 OABL, 9 IOI, 6 RLH and 11 normal controls. Transcriptomic data were available for 48 patients: 31 OABL and 17 controls. There was no experimental treatment group. Relative quantitative proteomics used five TMTpro16 batches (A-E); the sample-to-channel assignments are documented in the deposited IPX0004253001 batchReadMe. Each batch has a 134N control channel, absent from the selected biological Result columns. The exact mathematical normalization and use of that control are not established by the map
Short Description: TMTpro-based quantitative proteomic profiling of 65 orbital tissue specimens comprising 39 ocular adnexal B-cell lymphomas, 15 inflammatory non-cancer controls and 11 normal orbital tissue controls. Proteomic data were integrated with transcriptomic data to investigate protein–mRNA concordance, alternative-splicing dysregulation and diagnostic biomarkers

Main_Finding: High global protein–mRNA concordance was associated with OABL recurrence. Alternative-splicing events were dysregulated, and ADAR was identified as a central oncogenic splicing regulator. DNAJC9 protein abundance and nuclear staining were increased in OABL, supporting DNAJC9 as a potential diagnostic marker, particularly for EMZL.

The 15 inflammatory controls cannot be represented correctly by the existing preCancer or healthy-control columns. Clinical treatment status before tissue collection is Not specified. The result matrix contains RefSeq accessions. For atlas categorization, the 15 inflammatory/reactive controls (9 idiopathic orbital inflammation and 6 reactive lymphoid hyperplasia specimens) are retained under Pre-cancer; this is a conditional atlas category and does not indicate confirmed precancerous lesions.
Quantification_Format: Relative protein abundance (original numeric scale)

Title: Proteogenomic Analysis of Human Colon Cancer Reveals New Therapeutic Opportunities
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary colon adenocarcinoma tissue; mostly matched normal adjacent colon tissue (NAT) controls
Disease Subtype: Colon adenocarcinoma
Experimental Design: Prospective CPTAC colon cancer study using TMT10 global proteome and IMAC-enriched phosphoproteome profiling of tumor and normal adjacent tissues. The current PDC global-proteome matrix contains 97 tumors and 100 normal adjacent tissue profiles from 101 biological donors, including 96 matched tumor–normal pairs. Samples were analyzed across 22 TMT10 plexes with a pooled internal reference in channel 131, using 12 bRPLC fractions for global proteomics and 6 IMAC-enriched fractions for phosphoproteomics, and integrated with whole-exome sequencing, copy-number analysis, RNA sequencing, microRNA sequencing, and tumor label-free proteomics
Short Description: Proteogenomic study of prospectively collected colon cancer tumors and predominantly paired normal adjacent tissues; identified cancer-associated proteins, phosphosites, candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets, including CDK2-associated Rb phosphorylation and glycolysis-linked immune suppression
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: First large-scale prospective CPTAC proteogenomic study of human colon cancer integrating TMT proteomics, phosphoproteomics, genomics, and transcriptomics. The study identified tumor-associated proteins and phosphosites, defined integrated molecular subtypes, linked Rb phosphorylation and glycolysis-driven immune suppression to colon cancer biology, and revealed clinically relevant therapeutic targets, neoantigens, and candidate biomarkers not detectable from genomics alone.
Data_Caveats: The current PDC global-proteome matrix contains 97 tumor and 100 normal adjacent tissue profiles from 101 biological donors, including 96 matched tumor–normal pairs, one tumor-only donor, and four normal-only donors. The publication initially enrolled 110 colon cancer patients, so the PDC matrix represents a subset of the collected cohort. Normal adjacent tissues are not independent healthy-donor controls and may contain field effects. TMT measurements are relative to the pooled ColonRef channel 131 and may be affected by interference-related ratio compression. Bulk-tissue profiling, missing mass-spectrometry values, and limited detection of low-abundance proteins restrict cell-type resolution and proteome coverage; proposed biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain largely hypothesis-generating.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic Characterization of Ovarian HGSC Implicates Mitotic Kinases, Replication Stress in Observed Chromosomal Instability
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary tumor tissue; normal fallopian tube (FT) tissue
Tissue: Ovary, uterine tube and peritoneum [archived tissue-of-origin categories; specimen sampling site not reported]
Disease Subtype: High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC)
Experimental Design: Prospective CPTAC2 ovarian HGSC study using TMT10 multiplex global proteome and phosphoproteome profiling across 12 study plexes with a pooled reference in channel 131. Global proteome fractions were analyzed on a Q Exactive Plus, whereas phosphoproteome fractions were analyzed on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos following IMAC enrichment. The publication cohort comprised 83 HGSC tumors and 20 fallopian tube controls, including 10 matched tumor–FT pairs, with integration of whole-exome sequencing and RNA sequencing under controlled ischemia time of no more than 30 minutes
Short Description: Proteogenomic characterization of prospectively collected ovarian HGSC samples and matched fallopian tube precursor tissues identifying replication stress, mitotic kinase activation, RB1 hyperphosphorylation, homologous repair deficiency-associated signaling, and chromosomal instability programs
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic and phosphoproteomic analysis demonstrated increased CDK1/CDK2/CDK4/CDK7 and AURKA signaling, replication stress-associated phosphorylation, RB1 hyperphosphorylation, chromosomal instability, and altered DNA repair pathways in HGSC relative to fallopian tube precursor tissue, suggesting therapeutic relevance of CDK and Aurora kinase inhibition.
Data_Caveats: The current PDC protein matrix contains 84 tumor and 19 fallopian tube profiles, whereas the publication cohort comprised 83 tumors and 20 fallopian tube samples, including 10 matched tumor–normal pairs. Five JHU quality-control profiles are present in the original result matrix but are excluded from the 103 biological profiles; the pooled PNNL-JHU reference serves as the TMT denominator and is not represented as a separate quantitative profile. Two fallopian tube samples, N02OV001 and N17OV001, were excluded from the publication’s tumor–normal comparisons following quality-control assessment, leaving 18 normal samples; N02OV001 is absent from the current PDC proteome matrix, whereas N17OV001 remains present. Isobaric TMT quantification may be affected by interference-related ratio compression despite extensive fractionation. Survival analysis could not be performed reliably because of limited follow-up and few outcome events. Tumor-versus-fallopian-tube comparisons may additionally reflect differences in epithelial, stromal, smooth-muscle, and immune-cell composition.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic Landscape of Breast Cancer Tumorigenesis and Targeted Therapy
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary breast tumor tissue; adjacent normal breast tissue
Disease Subtype: PAM50 subtypes: Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, Basal-like, and Normal-like; clinical hormone-receptor/HER2 groups and triple-negative breast cancer were also analyzed
Experimental Design: CPTAC breast cancer global proteome profiling using TMT10-based LC-MS/MS across 17 plexes. Plexes 1–13 and 16–17 contained tumor samples, whereas plexes 14–15 contained 18 normal adjacent tissue profiles. Nine individual samples and a tumor-derived common reference were included in each TMT10 plex. Samples were fractionated by basic reversed-phase liquid chromatography and analyzed by Orbitrap Fusion Lumos MS2 acquisition with Spectrum Mill processing and two-component normalization. The publication’s integrated analyses included 122 tumors and excluded the normal adjacent tissue plexes after quality-control failure
Short Description: Large-scale CPTAC breast cancer proteome study using TMT10 multiplex quantitative proteomics of primary breast tumors. Global proteome analysis included extensive peptide fractionation, pooled internal reference channels, Orbitrap Fusion DDA acquisition, and CDAP-based protein quantification for integrated proteogenomic characterization
Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to ref
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated CPTAC proteogenomic analysis of treatment-naïve breast cancers refined molecular subtype classification beyond standard clinical markers, identified proteome-defined signaling and immune subgroups, revealed discordance between genomic and proteomic tumor classification, and identified candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities associated with immune checkpoint activity and CDK4/6 inhibitor responsiveness.
Data_Caveats: All 18 normal adjacent tissue profiles were analyzed in separate NAT-only TMT plexes and exhibited a systematic retention-time-dependent increase in TMT ratios consistent with a desalting-related chromatographic failure. These profiles did not meet quality standards and were excluded from subsequent analyses; consequently, the publication does not provide a validated quantitative tumor-versus-NAT comparison. Three proteome-profiled tumors were also excluded from full multi-omics integration because of low-quality RNA sequencing, leaving 122 tumors. MS2-based TMT quantification may remain susceptible to precursor co-isolation and ratio compression, although PSMs with precursor purity below 50% were excluded. Bulk cryopulverized tissue lacks spatial and cellular resolution, and the reported therapeutic associations are hypothesis-generating rather than direct evidence of clinical response.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic Characterization of Endometrial Carcinoma

Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C), TMT (K/N-term); Variable: Oxidation (M)

Nine tumor profiles were excluded from the publication’s downstream analyses, leaving 95 tumors and 49 normal tissue profiles. The normal comparator group included heterogeneous enriched endometrium, mixed endometrium-myometrium, and myometrium samples, with some normal profiles represented by pooled NX samples. Title: Integrated Proteogenomic Characterization of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma

Title: Integrative analysis of lung adenocarcinoma across diverse ethnicities and exposures

Title: Integrated Proteogenomic Characterization of HBV-Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma

Tissue: Liver tumor tissue; adjacent non-tumorous liver tissue
Disease Subtype: Hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma
Experimental Design: Tandem mass tag 11-plex global proteome and phosphoproteome profiling integrated with whole-exome sequencing and RNA sequencing of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma tumors and adjacent non-tumorous liver tissues. Global proteome samples were analyzed using a Q Exactive HF, while phosphopeptides were analyzed using an Orbitrap Fusion. The publication’s integrated analysis included 159 quality-controlled tumor–non-tumor pairs. The publication reports 165 patients and 330 tissue samples (165 tumors and 165 adjacent non-tumorous tissues). The export contains 170 case identifiers, including 160 with clinical data and ten with incomplete clinical annotation. The clinical table additionally contains the technical MIX record, which is not a participant or a separate Result profile. Original case identifiers are retained without inferred merging. Short Description: First integrated proteogenomic characterization of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma identifying proteomic subgroups associated with survival, metabolic reprogramming, microenvironment dysregulation, and CTNNB1-associated ALDOA phosphorylation signaling
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio to pooled ref
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: First integrated proteogenomic characterization of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma identified three proteomic subgroups associated with patient survival, liver-specific metabolic reprogramming, tumor microenvironment dysregulation, and proliferation; CTNNB1 mutation-associated ALDOA phosphorylation was shown to promote glycolysis and tumor cell proliferation.
Data_Caveats: Adjacent histologically non-tumorous liver tissues rather than liver tissues from independent healthy donors were used as controls and may retain hepatitis B virus-associated, inflammatory, cirrhotic, or field-effect alterations. The publication’s integrated analysis was limited to 159 quality-controlled tumor–non-tumor pairs from the 165-patient proteomics cohort. All patients in the principal cohort were hepatitis B virus-positive and were recruited from a surgically treated Chinese hepatocellular carcinoma population, limiting generalizability to non-hepatitis B virus-associated hepatocellular carcinoma and other populations. The molecular subgroups and therapeutic hypotheses require independent validation. Ten liver tissue samples (five tumors and five adjacent non-tumorous tissues) have incomplete clinical annotation, including missing age and sex information. Their tissue type is reported, but patient-level pairing could not be resolved from the available metadata. These samples were retained in the atlas.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic and metabolomic characterization of human glioblastoma
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary glioblastoma tumor tissue; normal brain tissue (GTEx)
Disease Subtype: Untreated glioblastoma with and without isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 and 2 mutations
Experimental Design: CPTAC glioblastoma discovery study using TMT11-based global proteome, phosphoproteome, and acetylome profiling of treatment-naïve primary GBM tissues and GTEx normal brain controls. Samples were analyzed by multidimensional LC-MS/MS with bRPLC fractionation and Orbitrap-based DDA acquisition. Integrated multi-omics analysis included whole-genome/exome sequencing, RNA-seq, single-nucleus RNA-seq, DNA methylation, lipidomics, and metabolomics to characterize signaling pathways, immune microenvironment, metabolic reprogramming, and subtype-specific molecular features in glioblastoma
Short Description: Comprehensive CPTAC proteogenomic and metabolomic characterization of human glioblastoma integrating proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome, genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics from treatment-naïve GBM tumors and normal brain tissues. Normalization Strategy: CDAP; median norm; log2 ratio to CompRef
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic and metabolomic profiling identified molecular subtypes of glioblastoma associated with survival, immune microenvironment remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and distinct signaling pathway activation patterns.
Data_Caveats: All normal brain controls were unmatched frontal cortex samples obtained from the Genotype-Tissue Expression Project rather than patient-matched adjacent tissues, introducing potential differences in donor composition, tissue procurement, processing, and molecular state relative to the glioblastoma specimens. Title: Integrative analysis of lung adenocarcinoma across diverse ethnicities and exposures

PDC000219 contributed to the broader multi-cohort analysis of molecular subtypes, smoking and carcinogen exposure, epidermal growth factor receptor signaling, mutational processes, immune states, and metabolic remodeling
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: In the integrated multi-cohort study, data from the Taiwanese cohort contributed to the identification of proteomic subtypes associated with genomic instability, epidermal growth factor receptor and smoking-related molecular features, carcinogen-associated mutational signatures, immune remodeling, metabolic dysregulation, and clinical outcome. These findings were derived from the combined international cohort and should not be attributed exclusively to PDC000219.
Data_Caveats: PDC000219 is one component of the larger integrated 2025 study and does not represent the complete 406-patient cohort. The metadata include lung squamous cell carcinoma and Other diagnostic annotations in addition to lung adenocarcinoma. The dataset contains 216 biological tissue samples from 108 patients: 108 tumors and 108 matched adjacent normal tissues. Repeated measurements yield 432 profiles and 864 columns comprising Log Ratio and Unshared Log Ratio. Adjacent normal tissues originate from the same patients; there is no independent healthy-donor cohort. Quantification is relative to a pooled TMT reference rather than absolute protein abundance. Five low-quality or corrupted raw mass spectrometry files were removed and one replacement file was added in study version 2.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Main_Finding: Early on-treatment biopsies from patients achieving pathological complete response showed greater suppression of ERBB2 protein, ERBB2 phosphosites, and downstream mTOR-target phosphosites. Proteogenomic analysis of non-pCR tumors identified several candidate resistance mechanisms, including false ERBB2 positivity without ERBB2 amplification, pseudo-ERBB2 positivity with insufficient ERBB2 protein activity, androgen-receptor signaling, mucin overexpression, EGFR-associated signaling, and an inactive or immune-desert tumor microenvironment.
Data_Caveats: This was a small proof-of-principle study: biopsies were available from 19 patients, but five cases were excluded because mean tumor content was below 50%, leaving 14 patients and 35 analyzed cores. The 35 cores are repeated measurements rather than independent patients and comprise 20 pre-treatment and 15 early on-treatment biopsies; duplicate cores were obtained for several patients and triplicate cores for one patient. The value 30 refers only to cores with successful RNA-seq, whereas MiProt proteomics succeeded for all 35 cores. PDC000325 contains the global proteome only, so findings requiring phosphoproteomics, WES, RNA-seq, or PDX experiments should not be attributed solely to this dataset. Treatments were not completely uniform, and two patients who did not receive pertuzumab were excluded from the paired differential analysis. CR4 and CR5 are technical reference materials, while Withdrawn is not a biological sample. The results are exploratory, not clinically actionable, and require validation in larger independent cohorts.

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of chemo-refractory high-grade serous ovarian cancer

Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: The independent FFPE validation cohort supported the predictive value of the 64-protein platinum-refractoriness panel. Because the FFPE validation data could not be directly aligned with the FFPE discovery dataset owing to the absence of a shared reference between the cohorts and the small cohort size, the model was re-estimated and evaluated using three-fold cross-validation within the 20 validation tumors. It achieved an AUC of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.84–1.00) and a sensitivity of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.40–1.00) at 98% specificity, supporting detection of a high-specificity subset of platinum-refractory HGSOCs.
Data_Caveats: PDC000358 is a small, balanced cohort of 20 primary FFPE tumors from 20 unique patients: 10 platinum-sensitive and 10 platinum-refractory cases. The FP-bridge entry is a pooled technical reference and must not be counted as a biological sample or patient. The reported AUC was obtained after re-estimating the model and applying three-fold cross-validation within this cohort, rather than by applying a completely locked discovery-cohort model, so performance may be optimistic. Treatment exposure is not recorded per sample in the local PDC annotation; pre-treatment status is based on the publication design. The PDC annotation includes one stage II case, whereas the publication describes the selected study population principally as stage III–IV. FFPE processing and bulk-tissue heterogeneity may affect protein coverage and abundance measurements, and the predictor requires additional prospective clinical validation.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Main_Finding: Main_FindingThe frozen validation cohort supported the 64-protein predictor of platinum refractoriness, with an AUC of 0.79 in the 35 patients independent of the FFPE discovery cohort and an AUC of 0.81 in the 29 overlapping patients. At 98% specificity, sensitivity was 25% and 43%, respectively, indicating that the predictor detects a specific subset rather than all refractory tumors. Five pathway-defined proteomic clusters were also reproduced, including metabolic, hypoxia/EMT/TGF-β, immune and cell-cycle-associated states. Extracellular-matrix-associated non-tryptic peptide patterns in clusters 4 and 5 were validated in the frozen cohort.
Data_Caveats: PDC000362 contains 72 biological measurements from 64 unique tumors because four tumors were analyzed in triplicate. Eight Cell_line-bridge channels and pooled Frozen-bridge references are technical controls and must not be counted as biological samples or patients. Twenty-nine of the 64 frozen cases overlap with the FFPE discovery cohort, leaving 35 fully non-overlapping validation cases. The protein model was developed in the FFPE discovery cohort and only evaluated in PDC000362; it is not yet a clinically validated predictor and detects only a subset of refractory tumors. Bulk-tissue heterogeneity and anatomical sampling site may influence measured protein abundance. Although samples were generally collected before adjuvant chemotherapy, 13 tumors across the broader publication cohort were later found to have received neoadjuvant chemotherapy; PDC000362 does not contain sufficient metadata for a reliable treated/untreated split.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Neoplastic cell enrichment of tumor tissues using coring and laser microdissection for proteomic and genomic analyses of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma

Disease Subtype: PDAC with variable neoplastic cellularity and stromal composition
Experimental Design: PDC000393 contains TMT10-based LC–MS/MS global proteome measurements for 27 biological tissue samples from six PDAC patients: 18 primary-tumor samples and 9 normal-adjacent pancreatic samples generated using bulk sectioning, tissue coring, and laser microdissection across three TMT10 plexes. The publication’s principal proteomic comparison was based on three paired PDAC/NAT cases; a separate WES analysis included eight PDAC tumors
Short Description: Comparative PDAC proteomics dataset examining how bulk sampling, tissue coring, and laser microdissection affect neoplastic-cell enrichment and measured protein composition. Paired tumor–NAT proteomic comparisons were available for three patients, while the PDC matrix additionally contains tumor samples from three further patients
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Laser microdissection produced the greatest enrichment of neoplastic cellularity and the most distinct proteomic profiles. Bulk and cored tissues showed comparatively similar protein patterns. LMD also increased KRAS mutation allele fractions, particularly in tumors with low initial neoplastic cellularity, whereas coring was less effective in such tumors. Sampling method affected the tumor-associated proteins detected; COL17A1, VSNL1, LYPD3, and VCAN were among the LMD-associated elevated proteins matching the Pancreatic Cancer Database.
Data_Caveats: PDC000393 contains 27 derived tissue samples from six biological patients, not 27 independent patients. The nine solid-tissue-normal samples are three bulk/cored/LMD preparations of matched normal-adjacent pancreas from three PDAC patients, not samples from nine healthy donors. The publication’s principal proteomic analysis included only three paired PDAC/NAT cases, while its KRAS/WES analysis included eight tumors; these publication-level cohort counts should not be equated with the six-patient PDC proteome dataset. The small paired proteomic cohort limits statistical power. Variable stromal content and neoplastic cellularity strongly influence bulk-tissue measurements. LMD yields limited material and may itself affect proteins or post-translational modifications, while coring is less effective for tumors with low cellularity. PDC annotation does not explicitly label the bulk, coring, and LMD relationships.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of lung adenocarcinoma reveals tumor heterogeneity, survival determinants, and therapeutically relevant pathways

Although selected candidate biomarkers were supported by IHC, RNA-ISH or external proteomic datasets, the authors indicate that further evaluation in independent cohorts is required before clinical application. Two additional reference entries (chRCC-ref-discovery-9 and chRCC-ref-discovery-10) are present in the PDC annotation but lack biological sample metadata and are excluded from the 68 biological samples.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Mapping the proteogenomic landscape enables prediction of drug response in acute myeloid leukemia

Short Description: Proteogenomic study of primary acute myeloid leukemia patient samples from the Beat AML cohort. Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).

Title: Integrated proteogenomic characterization of glioblastoma evolution

Disease Subtype: Glioblastoma multiforme; longitudinal primary and recurrent glioblastoma

Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Global proteome analysis revealed a marked molecular transition from primary to recurrent glioblastoma. The 221 biological profiles correspond to 214 unique tumor aliquots because four primary aliquots and three recurrent aliquots were measured twice. A total of 104 patients have paired primary and recurrent tumors, four patients have primary-tumor profiles only, and one patient has a recurrent-tumor profile only. The patients.csv file contains 111 records, including 109 glioblastoma patients and two non-biological records, ref and Other. No healthy or adjacent-normal brain controls are included. Recurrent tumors were collected after treatment, so primary–recurrent differences reflect both tumor evolution and therapeutic selection. Conclusions requiring genomic, transcriptomic, phosphoproteomic, or longitudinal clinical integration extend beyond the global-proteome component deposited in PDC000514.

Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).

The cohort comprises 105 patients with paired tumor and matched/adjacent normal tissues, corresponding to 210 unique biological tissue specimens. One patient, OCM042, is annotated with disease_type = Other rather than Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma; this patient contributes two unique tissue specimens represented by four quantitative profiles. Excluding OCM042 leaves 104 OSCC patients, 208 unique tumor/normal tissue specimens, and 444 quantitative biological profiles. Matched normal tissues were obtained from the same cancer patients and are not independent healthy-donor controls. Pooled tissue and pooled cell-line reference channels are technical normalization materials and must not be counted as biological samples or patients.

Title: Integrative analysis of lung adenocarcinoma across diverse ethnicities and exposures

Experimental Design: TMT10-based quantitative global proteome profiling of paired primary lung tumor and matched normal adjacent tissue (NAT) samples from the Taiwanese ICPC-B cohort; 124 patients and 248 tissue samples analyzed across 31 TMT10 plexes, with reference samples included for quality control
Short Description: Global proteome profiling of the ICPC-B cohort comprising 124 paired lung tumor–NAT cases (98 LUAD, 13 LSCC, and 13 other lung tumors). Samples were analyzed using TMT10-based LC-MS/MS and integrated with genomic, transcriptomic, and phosphoproteomic data in the associated multi-cohort proteogenomic study of lung adenocarcinoma
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT10 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Within the integrated multi-cohort lung cancer analysis, the Taiwanese ICPC-B cohort contributed paired tumor and normal-adjacent-tissue proteomic data from 124 patients, including 98 lung adenocarcinomas, 13 lung squamous cell carcinomas, and 13 other lung tumor types. The broader study identified molecular features associated with EGFR and KRAS alterations, chromosomal instability, immune signaling, carcinogen-exposure signatures, and early-stage tumors with late-stage-like characteristics, and proposed IGF2BP3 as a candidate biomarker of highly fragmented, genomically unstable tumors. These integrated findings derive from the combined 406-patient cohort and should not be attributed exclusively to PDC000563.
Data_Caveats: PDC000563 represents the Academia Sinica LUAD ICPC-B proteome component, but the associated publication integrates multiple related PDC datasets from CPTAC and ICPC Academia Sinica programs. Therefore, conclusions from the paper refer to the broader 406-patient multi-cohort LUAD analysis, not only to PDC000563. Related studies include CPTAC LUAD proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome and ubiquitylome datasets, as well as Academia Sinica LUAD100 proteome/phosphoproteome and ICPC-B phosphoproteome datasets. Taiwanese IR was used as a bridging internal reference for cross-cohort comparison. For the curated biospecimen count, use the project-level tissue annotation separately from the publication-level integrated cohort size.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of the CALGB 40601 (Alliance) HER2+ breast cancer neoadjuvant trial reveals resistance biomarkers
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Pretreatment needle-core biopsies from primary HER2-positive breast invasive carcinoma tumors; fresh-frozen OCT-embedded tumor tissue; no cell lines; no mouse samples
Disease Subtype: HER2-positive breast cancer; neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy cohort
Experimental Design: TMT16-based proteomic analysis of pretreatment primary tumor biopsies from patients with HER2-positive breast cancer enrolled in the CALGB 40601 neoadjuvant trial. The PDC proteome dataset includes 59 cases and 80 aliquots, analyzed across 5 TMT16 plexes with 24 fractions per plex. The study was designed to identify protein-level biomarkers associated with pathological complete response versus non-pCR after anti-HER2 therapy
Short Description: Proteomic profiling of pretreatment HER2-positive breast cancer biopsies from the CALGB 40601 trial identified resistance-associated features, including lack of ERBB2 amplification/HER2 protein overexpression in some non-pCR cases and increased EMT, Notch, and WNT/β-catenin signaling in non-pCR tumors. GPRC5A and TPBG were validated as reproducible markers associated with lack of pathological complete response
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT16 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteogenomic profiling of pretreatment HER2-positive breast cancer biopsies identified molecular features associated with resistance to neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy. Lack of ERBB2 amplification and HER2 protein overexpression was associated with non-pCR, indicating that some tumors classified as HER2-positive by standard clinical testing may represent potential false-positive cases. Among proteogenomics-confirmed HER2-positive tumors, non-pCR was associated with increased extracellular matrix, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, WNT/β-catenin, cell-lineage and tumor-microenvironment-related signaling. Twenty-four pCR-associated proteins were reproduced in an independent proteomic dataset, and GPRC5A, TPBG, SP140L and NEU1 were significant in a third proteomic cohort. Meta-analysis of ten treatment regimens from four independent studies confirmed higher GPRC5A and TPBG mRNA expression in non-pCR tumors.
Data_Caveats: PDC000582 contains pretreatment tumor biopsies only, with no healthy controls or matched adjacent normal tissue. The quantitative matrix contains 75 clinical Log Ratio columns representing 75 needle-core biopsies from 54 patients; 33 patients contributed one biopsy and 21 contributed two biopsies. Raw PDC metadata list 59 cases and 80 aliquots because they additionally include five technical common-reference entities, TBNC_CR_1–TBNC_CR_5, corresponding to one pooled reference per TMT16 plex. These reference entities are not clinical donors or biological samples. Separately, the article reports that 80 clinical biopsies from 54 patients passed proteogenomic quality control, of which 75 yielded TMT-based proteomic and phosphoproteomic data. Thus, the 80 raw PDC aliquots and the 80 QC-passed clinical biopsies reported in the article are numerically equal but do not represent the same composition. The corresponding Unshared Log Ratio columns are an alternative quantification metric, not additional samples. PDC000582 contains the global proteome arm, whereas phosphoproteomic data are deposited separately as PDC000583. Response associations are correlative, duplicate biopsies originate from the same tumors, and statistical power is limited within individual treatment arms; the lapatinib-only arm was excluded from downstream comparative analyses because of its small sample size. Validation results from independent proteomic and transcriptomic cohorts extend beyond the PDC000582 dataset.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic analysis of enriched HGSOC tumor epithelium identifies prognostic signatures and therapeutic vulnerabilities
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Bulk high-grade serous carcinoma tumor tissue; laser microdissection-enriched high-grade serous carcinoma tumor epithelium; laser microdissection-enriched stromal compartment in a subset
Tissue: High-grade serous carcinoma tumor tissue from ovary, peritoneum, and abdominal/metastatic sites
Disease Subtype: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC; APOLLO-2 cohort)
Experimental Design: TMT11-based global proteome profiling of untreated high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma tumors, including matched bulk tumor tissue and laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelial fractions; integrated with whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, reverse phase protein array data, tumor purity assessment, homologous recombination deficiency/proficiency classification, and survival analysis
Short Description: Proteogenomic study of 70 chemo-naive high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma tumors from primary/adnexal and metastatic sites. The study compared bulk tumor tissue with laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelium to evaluate how tumor purity, stromal admixture, immune infiltration, molecular subtype reclassification, homologous recombination deficiency-associated metabolic pathways, and BMI1 expression relate to prognosis and therapeutic vulnerability
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: In the full APOLLO-2 study, laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelium increased tumor purity and improved the detection of somatic variants, structural variants, and predicted neoepitopes compared with bulk tumor. Mesenchymal subtype assignments in bulk tumors were strongly influenced by stromal admixture and frequently changed after epithelial enrichment. Longer progression-free survival was associated with immune- and TIL-related proteomic signatures. HRD tumor epithelium showed enrichment of mitochondrial metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation pathways. HRP tumors exhibited increased BMI1 expression, which was associated with poorer outcomes, and HRP HGSOC cell models showed greater sensitivity to BMI1 inhibitors.
Data_Caveats: PDC000585 contains only the non-enriched/bulk tumor proteome arm of the APOLLO-2 study, not the complete set of bulk, laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelial and stromal proteomes described in the article. The analytical cohort comprises 70 chemo-naive HGSOC tumors from 70 patients, including 49 primary/adnexal and 21 metastatic tumors. Raw PDC metadata list 72 cases and 72 aliquots because they additionally include one pooled-reference entity and one Withheld entity; atlas analysis retains only the 70 clinically annotated tumor samples. The quantitative matrix contains 120 Log Ratio columns: 70 clinical samples and 50 Withheld/unassigned TMT channels, which are excluded from biological analysis. The corresponding Unshared Log Ratio columns are an alternative quantification metric, not additional samples. Samples are tumor-only, with no healthy or precancer controls. The full article additionally analyzed matched laser microdissection-enriched tumor epithelium and stromal fractions from a subset, while findings from LMD comparisons, independent validation cohorts and BMI1 inhibitor experiments in cell models extend beyond the PDC000585 proteome arm.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic characterization of non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors unravels clinically relevant subgroups
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Paired primary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm tumor tissue and matched/adjacent solid normal tissue: pancreas 16 pairs; colorectal 12; stomach 8; small intestine 1
Tumor Type: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors and neuroendocrine carcinomas
Disease Subtype: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (25 pairs: pancreas 14, extra-pancreatic 11); neuroendocrine carcinoma, NOS (12 pairs: pancreas 2, extra-pancreatic 10)
Experimental Design: TMT16-based global proteome profiling of 37 paired GEP-NEN tumors and matched/adjacent normal tissues across six TMT16 plexes; trypsin digestion; iodoacetamide alkylation; high-pH reversed-phase fractionation; Q Exactive HF-X; DDA-HCD; MS2 reporter-ion quantification
Short Description: Proteome PhaseII arm of a proteogenomic NF-PanNET discovery study. The usable pancreatic cohort in this PDC part includes paired primary pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and matched solid normal pancreatic tissue; the broader study integrates genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic and phosphoproteomic data to define molecular subgroups, prognostic proteins and therapeutic vulnerabilities
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT16 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Integrated proteogenomic analysis identified MEN1-associated functional effects, including CENPV; a prognostic GNAO1–INA–VCAN signature; four proteomic/phosphoproteomic subtypes; and candidate vulnerabilities including CDK5 and subtype-specific CACNA1D targeting.
Data_Caveats: PDC000588 is a multisite Phase II GEP-NEN cohort, not a pancreas-only 37-pair NF-PanNET cohort or the complete 108-case multi-omic cohort described in the article. Raw PDC metadata list 53 cases and 94 aliquots. The quantitative result matrix contains 88 aliquots: 74 biological samples representing 37 complete tumor–normal pairs and 14 NR/Other non-clinical technical channels. Six additional NR/Other technical/reference IDs are present only in the patient metadata and have no corresponding quantitative columns. Qualification status is not included in result_PDC000588.xlsx and therefore cannot be inferred from the quantitative file. Matched solid-normal tissues represent patient-matched adjacent controls rather than independent healthy donors. Accordingly, the atlas analysis includes 37 clinical donors and 74 biological samples, whereas Samples Original N and Samples Used N are 88 and 74, respectively.
Quantification_Format: TMT reporter-ion relative quantification; protein-level log2 ratios

Title: Proteogenomic characterization of non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors unravels clinically relevant subgroups
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary NF-PanNET tumor tissue and matched normal-adjacent pancreatic tissue (NAT)
Tumor Type: Non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor / well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
Disease Subtype: Non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors / NF-PanNETs; mostly well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, G1–G3
Experimental Design: TMT11-based global proteome profiling of primary NF-PanNET tumors and matched/adjacent normal pancreatic tissues; isobaric MS2 reporter ion quantitation, 2D-LC-MS/MS, high-pH reversed-phase fractionation followed by nanoLC-MS/MS; DDA-HCD on Q Exactive HF-X; MS2 reporter-ion quantification
Short Description: Proteome Phase I discovery cohort for molecular characterization of NF-PanNETs. Dataset includes pancreatic primary tumor and solid tissue normal samples; used to support proteomic stratification, prognostic protein signatures, and therapeutic vulnerability analysis
Normalization Strategy: Median norm; log2 ratio
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C); TMT11 labeling (K, peptide N-terminus). Variable: Oxidation (M).
Main_Finding: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling identified therapeutic vulnerabilities associated with ubiquitous CDK5 activation and C2-specific upregulation of CACNA1D phosphorylation.
Data_Caveats: PDC000590 is Proteome Phase I only. Although the study description mentions genomics, transcriptomics, phosphoproteomics, mouse models, PDOs and xenografts, these are not all contained in this PDC entry. Biospecimens include Primary Tumor and Solid Tissue Normal pancreas samples, plus M1–M23 Not Reported / Other samples. Clinical metadata describe NF-PanNET cases, mostly well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with grades G1–G3 and stages I–IV, but part of cases have grade/stage/morphology as Not Reported. Some samples are marked Disqualified, so counts should be checked separately for total vs usable samples

Title: Proteomics Profiling of CLL Versus Healthy B-cells Identifies Putative Therapeutic Targets and a Subtype-independent Signature of Spliceosome Dysregulation
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Primary peripheral-blood B-cell samples from 14 patients in the study's CLL cohort; three healthy-donor B-cell samples were used as comparison and inter-batch bridging controls but are not separate profiles in the selected matrix.
Disease Subtype: IGHV-mutated, IGHV-unmutated, Trisomy 12, NOTCH1-mutant, SF3B1-mutant, CD38+
Experimental Design: Two TMT 10-plex experiments comparing primary CLL B-cells with three individual healthy-donor B-cell controls shared across both batches. The selected matrix contains 14 patient profiles: seven without and seven with prior clinical treatment; no experimental perturbation.
Short Description: Protein-level profiling of isolated peripheral-blood B-cells from the study's CLL cohort. The selected Table S2 export contains 14 patient profiles, including outlier 4621. The discovery cohort comprised 14 patients and three healthy donors (17 participants). Donors 1, 2 and 3 occupy 126, 127N and 127C in both batches; they are individual bridging controls, not a pooled reference. Modifications: Fixed: Methylthio (C); TMT (K, Protein N-term). Variable: TMT (Y); Oxidation (M); Deamidation (N, Q); Phosphorylation (S, T, Y)
Main_Finding: Proteomic profiling identified a CLL-associated signature of increased mRNA-processing and spliceosome proteins across molecular subtypes. The study also highlighted candidate therapeutic targets and previously underrecognized surface markers.
Data_Caveats: Small, clinically heterogeneous cohort with mixed prior-treatment histories and limited power for subtype comparisons. The selected matrix contains processed patient-to-control ratios without separate healthy-donor profiles and retains the author-designated outlier 4621.
Quantification_Format: Dimensionless log2(CLL/HDB) values after minimum-fold-change selection across three individual healthy-donor controls.

Title: Nicotine-induced protein expression profiling reveals mutually altered proteins across four human cell lines

Tissue: Cultured HEK293, HeLa, RLT-PSC and SH-SY5Y cells

Title: Quantitative proteomic analysis of prostate tissue specimens identifies deregulated protein complexes in primary prostate cancer

Title: Global analysis of methionine oxidation provides a census of folding stabilities for the human proteome

Main_Finding: Proteome-wide HR-SPROX quantified local protein folding stability in HCA2-hTert human fibroblast lysates. Data_Caveats: HR-SPROX study of protein folding stability; selected subset contains one HCA2-hTert lysate control without GdmCl, H2O2 or TMAO. hTERT-expressing fibroblasts are a cell-line model, not primary cells or healthy donor samples; Control Healthy is an atlas category. First accession represents a MaxQuant protein group. Atlas filtering excludes full groups containing REV__ or CON__ before first-accession selection, plus MaxQuant flagged/empty-ID rows. One profile cannot estimate biological variability or support disease/treatment comparisons. Whole-study folding-stability findings are not derived from this control alone.
Quantification_Format: Arbitrary units: MaxQuant isotope-corrected reporter-ion intensity at protein-group level, reporter index 0. Not fraction oxidized, folding energy or absolute protein concentration.

Disease Subtype: Intestinal and Diffuse subtypes
Experimental Design: Paired tumor and adjacent normal tissue profiling from ten gastric cancer patients: five diffuse and five intestinal cases analyzed in separate TMT 10-plex experiments.
Short Description: TMT 10-plex LC-MS/MS profiling of 20 fresh-frozen gastric tissue specimens from ten patients who did not receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The selected matrix contains ten paired protein-abundance ratios.
TMT Channels Used: Diffuse subtype Sample Identifier Tumor Adjacent norrmal Patient 1 126 127N Patient 2 127C 128N Patient 3 128C 129N Patient 4 129C 130N Patient 5 130C 131 Intestinal subtype Sample Identifier Tumor Adjacent norrmal Patient 1 126 129N Patient 2 127N 129C Patient 3 127C 130N Patient 4 128N 130C Patient 5 128C 131
Normalization Strategy: Relative TMT reporter ion quantification; paired two-tailed t-test; ≥2-fold change threshold; Perseus statistical analysis
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C), TMT 10-plex (N-term, K); Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Subtype-specific signatures: GREM1, BAG2, OLFM4, TRIP6 in diffuse; MAGE-A9 in intestinal; mRNA-protein correlation diffuse r=0.46, intestinal r=0.28
Data_Caveats: Adjacent normal tissues were collected from the same cancer patients, not healthy donors. The selected matrix contains ten paired ratios rather than twenty separate tissue-abundance profiles. The first diffuse-subtype ratio has conflicting direction annotations in Supplementary Table S3.
Quantification_Format: Protein abundance ratios between paired tumor and adjacent normal tissues.

Title: Glioblastoma stem cells express non-canonical proteins and exclusive mesenchymal-like or non-mesenchymal-like protein signatures
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Six patient-derived glioblastoma stem-cell lines, the T98G glioblastoma cell line and primary human astrocytes.
Cell Line Name: BT273; BT373; BT379; BT417; BT462; BT517; T98G; primary human astrocytes
Cell Line Cancer;Normal: Cancer; Cancer; Cancer; Cancer; Cancer; Cancer; Cancer; Normal
Tumor type for cell lines: Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma; Glioblastoma; Normal
Disease Subtype: Proneural and classical transcriptomic subtypes in the six BT glioblastoma stem-cell lines.
Experimental Design: Comparative proteomic profiling of six BT glioblastoma stem-cell lines and T98G in biological triplicate, with primary human astrocytes measured in technical triplicate, using three TMT 10-plex sets with two pooled internal standards per set.
Short Description: HiRIEF LC-MS/MS profiling of 24 cell-culture profiles comprising 18 BT glioblastoma stem-cell profiles, three T98G profiles and three technical measurements of one astrocyte biological sample.
TMT Channels Used: TMT_label Set1 Set2 Set3 127N T98GA BT373A BT379C 127C BT517B BT417B BT462C 128N BT379A T98GC BT417C 128C BT462A BT273B BT517A 129N BT462B BT517C BT379B 129C BT373B astrocyteA BT273A 130N BT273C BT417A astrocyteC 130C astrocyteB BT373C T98GB
TMT Additional Channels: 126 I.S. A I.S. A I.S. A 131 I.S. B I.S. B I.S. B
Normalization Strategy: Median of PSM ratios with internal standards
Modifications: Carbamidomethyl(C); Oxidation(M); TMT
Main_Finding: Comparison with T98G and primary human astrocytes identified a shared glioblastoma stem-cell-associated protein signature. Proteomic profiling also revealed differences between transcriptomic subtype assignments and protein-level subtype enrichment.
Data_Caveats: Astrocyte controls comprise three technical measurements of one biological sample, whereas BT glioblastoma stem-cell lines and T98G were measured in biological triplicate. Culture conditions differed between cell types. Counts represent cultured-cell profiles rather than independent patients.

Title: Glioblastoma stem cells express non-canonical proteins and exclusive mesenchymal-like or non-mesenchymal-like protein signatures
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Patient-derived glioblastoma stem cell cultures from the HGCC panel: 11 cell lines represented by 14 quantitative profiles, including duplicate measurements of U3452, U3071MG and U3053MG.
Disease Subtype: Proneural/classical-like and mesenchymal-like glioblastoma stem cell phenotypes.
Experimental Design: Whole-proteome profiling of 11 HGCC glioblastoma stem cell lines in one TMTpro 16-plex. Three lines were measured in duplicate, yielding 14 sample profiles across 16 TMT channels. Channels 133C and 134N were left empty, and no internal standard was included.
Short Description: HiRIEF LC–MS/MS profiling of patient-derived HGCC glioblastoma stem cell cultures using 72 peptide fractions and a Q Exactive HF to characterize proneural/classical-like and mesenchymal-like protein signatures.
Normalization Strategy: Median of PSM ratios (OpenMS IsobaricAnalyzer)
Modifications: Carbamidomethyl(C); Oxidation(M); TMTpro
Main_Finding: The HGCC panel supported separation of mesenchymal-like glioblastoma stem cells from proneural/classical-like cells using the GSC-associated protein signature. GPC-like and GM-like signatures showed opposing enrichment patterns, and GM-like cells showed enrichment of hypoxia-associated gene sets.
Data_Caveats: Fourteen quantitative profiles represent eleven patient-derived cell lines, with duplicate measurements of three lines. These profiles are not independent clinical patient samples. The biological or technical nature of the duplicates is not specified in Supplementary Table S2. Channels 133C and 134N were empty, and no internal standard was included. Cancer Untreated denotes the atlas cell-model category and does not establish donor treatment history.
Quantification_Format: Author-supplied relative TMT protein-expression values

Title: Glioblastoma stem cells express non-canonical proteins and exclusive mesenchymal-like or non-mesenchymal-like protein signatures
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Frozen glioblastoma tissue specimens: seven primary tumors, including one highly necrotic specimen, and three non-matched recurrent tumors.
Disease Subtype: Primary glioblastoma (7); recurrent glioblastoma (3).
Experimental Design: Unpaired whole-proteome profiling of ten glioblastoma tissue specimens in one TMT 10-plex: seven primary tumors, including one highly necrotic specimen, and three recurrent tumors; no internal standard.
Short Description: HiRIEF LC–MS/MS profiling of ten frozen glioblastoma tissue specimens on a Q Exactive HF to compare relative protein-expression profiles between primary and non-paired recurrent tumors.
TMT Channels Used: TMT_label lab_id tumour_type 126 GCH_002 primary 127C GCH_004 primary - necrotic 128N GCH_007 primary 129C GCH_012 primary 130N GCH_014 primary 130C GCH_015 primary 131 GCH_016 primary
TMT Channels Comparison: 127N GCH_003 recurrent 128C GCH_009 recurrent 129N GCH_010 recurrent
Normalization Strategy: Median of PSM ratios (OpenMS IsobaricAnalyzer)
Modifications: Carbamidomethyl(C); Oxidation(M); TMT
Main_Finding: Recurrent glioblastoma tumors showed activation of the mesenchymal-like GM protein signature and suppression of the GPC-like signature; the GM-like signature was also associated with tumor necrosis.
Data_Caveats: The matrix contains ten glioblastoma tissue specimens classified in the atlas as ten patients: seven primary and three non-paired recurrent tumors. Sample-level treatment history is unavailable; therefore, assignment of all ten profiles to Cancer Untreated is an atlas classification and does not establish that the recurrent tumors were treatment-naive. The article directly reports ten specimens but does not provide a specimen-to-patient crosswalk. One primary tumor was highly necrotic, and the TMT 10-plex contained no internal standard.
Quantification_Format: Author-supplied relative protein-expression values derived from TMT PSM ratios; signed values copied unchanged; exact transformation and ratio denominator not explicitly documented.

Title: ATM inhibition enhances the efficacy of radiation across distinct molecular subgroups of pediatric high-grade glioma
Tissue Cell Type Detailed: Cultured diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma cells: SJ-DIPG7, SJ-DIPG29 and SU-DIPG-XIII; whole-cell proteome.
Tumor type for cell lines: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma; Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma; Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
Disease Subtype: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma with H3.3 K27M mutation
Experimental Design: TMTpro 16-plex whole-proteome profiling of three cultured diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma models at 0 Gy and 4 Gy. Eight profiles: one per dose for SJ-DIPG7 and SU-DIPG-XIII, and two per dose for SJ-DIPG29. Cells were harvested 2 h after irradiation.
Short Description: Whole-cell proteomic profiling of SJ-DIPG7, SJ-DIPG29 and SU-DIPGXIII cells before irradiation and after 4 Gy irradiation, using TMTpro labeling and Q Exactive HF mass spectrometry. Protein intensities were selected from the deposited WHL export.
TMT Channels Used: SJ-DIPG7 + SJ-DIPG29(rep1,rep2) + SU-DIPGXIII
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C), TMT (K, N-term); Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: ATM inhibition with AZD1390 enhanced the response to radiation across distinct molecular subgroups of pediatric high-grade glioma in preclinical models.
Data_Caveats: Eight quantitative profiles represent three cultured tumor cell-line models, not independent patients. The two SJ-DIPG29 profiles per dose are not classified as biological or technical replicates. The 0 Gy channel assignments are supported by direct matching to Supplementary Table S4B; 4 Gy assignments use shared channel labels, the S4A phosphoproteome mapping and S5 comparison pairs. All matrix intensities come from the WHL export. The article reports collection 2 h after irradiation, whereas S5A/S5B titles state 1 h; collection time remains unresolved. NHA controls and phosphopeptide measurements are excluded. The selected data include UCSC entries and contaminants.
Quantification_Format: Linear protein-level TMTpro reporter-ion intensities; source values retained.

Tissue: Cultured OCI-AML8227 leukemia cells; bone marrow denotes model origin, not directly measured marrow tissue
Disease Subtype: Acute myeloid leukemia cell-culture model with CD34+CD38− stem-like, CD34+CD38+ progenitor-like and CD34− blast populations; clinical molecular subtype not reported.
Experimental Design: Selected dataset: RTS-SPS-MS3 with a 750 ms maximum ion injection time. Experimental Design: Multiregion proteomic profiling of laser-microdissected tumor epithelium and stroma from primary-disease, relapse and autopsy specimens using 14 TMTpro 16-plex experiments.
Short Description: Proteomic profiling of 105 FFPE tissue specimens from 15 women with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, yielding 102 tumor epithelial and 94 stromal profiles. The selected matrix includes 40 profiles collected during primary disease, eight at relapse and 148 at autopsy. Matched epithelial and stromal profiles are available for 91 specimens; 11 have epithelial profiles only and three have stromal profiles only.
Modifications: Fixed: Carbamidomethyl (C), TMTpro (K, N-term); Variable: Oxidation (M)
Main_Finding: Proteomic analysis revealed substantial heterogeneity within individual patients: tumor epithelial profiles clustered primarily by patient, whereas stromal profiles clustered by anatomical site. Compared with primary and recurrent specimens, autopsy stromal samples showed increased abundance of proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation and glucose metabolism; a smaller subset of oxidative phosphorylation proteins was also increased in tumor epithelium. The broader multiomic analysis demonstrated polyclonal end-stage disease with multiple coexisting resistance mechanisms, including restoration of homologous recombination, together with changes in immune composition consistent with immune escape.
Data_Caveats: The 102 tumor profiles are assigned to Case Cancer Untreated by atlas convention; this does not establish absence of prior treatment. The 94 Control Healthy profiles represent stromal tissue from the same patients with cancer, not healthy donors. Multiple profiles originate from the same patients. The selected matrix contains linear PSM-summed protein abundances without cross-plex normalization.
Quantification_Format: Linear protein-level abundances derived from summed TMTpro reporter-ion intensities

All six profiles are assigned to Case Cancer Untreated solely under the atlas convention for grouping benign disease specimens within the cancer categories and assigning cases without confirmed treatment information to the untreated category. This assignment does not establish malignancy, a precancerous state or treatment-naive status; the zero Case Cancer Treated count reflects this convention. Fibrous dysplasia is a developmental disorder, whereas cemento-ossifying fibroma is a benign neoplasm. Diagnosis and anatomical site are confounded: all fibrous dysplasia specimens originated from the maxilla and all cemento-ossifying fibroma specimens from the mandible. The selected matrix contains linear normalized abundances; the publication applied additional log2 transformation and median subtraction for statistical analysis.
Quantification_Format: Linear normalized protein abundances.

Experimental Design: Three healthy donors measured under three conditions: unstimulated control, 24-hour PMA/ionomycin stimulation and 24-hour anti-CD3/CD28 stimulation. The nine profiles are repeated condition-specific measurements from three donors rather than nine independent donors
Short Description: TMTpro global-proteome profiling of resting and activated primary human peripheral-blood T cells; part of an integrated proteogenomic study of canonical proteins and microproteins

Data_Caveats: The global-proteome matrix contains nine profiles representing three healthy donors measured under three conditions: unstimulated control, 24-hour PMA/ionomycin stimulation and 24-hour anti-CD3/CD28 stimulation. These profiles are repeated condition-specific measurements from three donors rather than nine independent donors. Donor age and sex are not reported. Exact TMTpro reporter-channel assignments and the detailed reporter-ion normalization procedure are not provided in the processed matrix. Findings concerning 411 microproteins additionally rely on nascent-proteome, RNA-seq, custom-database and functional-validation experiments outside this canonical global-proteome matrix.
